text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTOPAGER -> PagerDuty PD-927361 fired for host gpux-17 (us-west2-gpu-rack-4). Symptoms: kernel panic detected on serial console, kubelet transitioned to NotReady. Auto-escalation threshold hit. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/hosts/gpux-17

pagerduty: PD-927361 acknowledged by @maya (sre, primary). Escalation timer paused.

maya: I'm taking this. pulling serial logs, checking node state. tagging @devon for infra if hardware > suspected.

maya: quick check: `kubectl get nodes | grep gpux-17`
```
gpux-17   NotReady    3d   v1.25.4   gpu,highmem   12m
```

devon: can you paste the dmesg from serial? if it's kernel panic we should cordon asap and start drain/evac.

maya: serial snippet (last lines):
```
[ 1234.567890] RIP: 0010:panic+0x1f/0x3a
[ 1234.567891] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
[ 1234.567892] Call Trace:
[ 1234.567893]  dump_stack+0x45/0x6a
...\n```

natalie: UI shows a small spike in 5xxs for the hosted API in us-west2 since 11:02. Affected model routes: "text-gen-prod-a" (10% error rate increase). Not yet customer-wide but some tail latency/failed requests.

eric: routing policy should fallback to compatible model on different hosts automatically, but if this node is part of a dedicated pool we might need to re-route capacity manually. @maya what's the pool?

maya: gpux-17 is in dedicated pool redwood-dedicated-usw2-g4-4. It's hosting 6 pods: model-runtime-* (3), monitoring-agent (1), node-exporter (1), kube-proxy (1).

devon: plan: 1) cordon gpux-17 2) drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-local-data 3) request hardware team to power-cycle and run vendor diagnostics 4) if drain stalls, force-evict and migrate replicas to cold pool.

maya: executing cordon/drain now:
```
kubectl cordon gpux-17
kubectl drain gpux-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

ops-bot: drain started for node gpux-17. 4 pods pending eviction, 2 DaemonSet-managed.

maya: drain is stuck on model-runtime-2 (CrashLoopBackOff). checking pod logs.

maya: model-runtime-2 logs show GPU driver reset errors:
```
E Driver: nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex failed: unknown error
E Model-runtime: failing healthcheck, restarting
```

devon: that looks hardware-level. I'm paging hardware team on-call and opening ticket INFRA-4342. @eric can you trigger route fallback for redwood-dedicated-usw2-g4-4? want to shift traffic off this pool for the next hour.

eric: doing a soft fallback now: updating smart-routing policy to de-prioritize redwood-dedicated-usw2-g4-4 for latency-sensitive routes. command:
```
redwoodctl routing set-priority --pool redwood-dedicated-usw2-g4-4 --priority low --routes "text-gen-prod-a,chat-prod"
```

eric: routing change applied. traffic shifting (gradual) to compatible pools. monitor for 5xx drop.

natalie: after change, 5xxs dropped to baseline within ~90s for text-gen-prod-a. still seeing increased latency for some debug customers. marking as partial-impact, not outage.

maya: drain completed for non-daemonset pods. model-runtime-2 evicted. starting node reprovision steps. leaving kubelet cordoned.

ops-bot: hardware ticket INFRA-4342 created and assigned to #infra-oncall, priority P1, ETA initial response 20m.

devon: I'll loop in hardware. recommend power-cycle and vendor diagnostics (nvme and gpu tests).

maya: summary for handoff: gpux-17 experienced kernel panic -> kubelet NotReady. Non-daemonset pods drained. Traffic fallback applied to avoid customer impact. Hardware ticket opened INFRA-4342. I'll follow for the next 30m and then hand off to night oncall. TODOs: confirm vendor diag, confirm node reprovision or reprovision onto replacement hw, verify telemetry over 1h.

maya: handing off to @priya (night oncall) at 2748003000. full context above.

priya: acked. I'll take post-incident monitoring and follow-up with infra for the vendor diag. will escalate back if we see error rate > 3% for > 15m.

natalie: adding note to incident tracker: impact=partial, services=text-gen-prod-a, mitigation=routing fallback + node drain, followup=hardware diag + possible reprovision.

sre-oncall: recommend we run a quick replay of cache warmup for fallback pools to reduce tail latency. scheduling a short job.

ops-bot: vendor on-call has accepted INFRA-4342 and scheduled remote diagnostics at 11:40 PT.

maya: leaving final logs and commands so handoff is clean:
```
# cordoned
kubectl get node gpux-17 -o yaml | grep -A3 conditions
# drained
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep gpux-17
# revert routing after resolution
redwoodctl routing set-priority --pool redwood-dedicated-usw2-g4-4 --priority normal
```

oncall-next: Thanks @maya, @priya. I'll monitor the routing metrics and customer tickets. If vendor confirms hardware failure, we'll reprovision with spare and rebuild node from image gpux-ami-v2.

incident-bot: PD-927361 status: acknowledged -> mitigation in place. No active alerts for gpux-17 in the last 5m. Will auto-close if stable for 30m.

priya: closing the loop after vendor diagnostics: they ran nvml tests and reported intermittent ECC errors on GPU0; recommended RMA. scheduling reprovision to spare host gpux-spare-09 and will reprovision gpux-17 after RMA.

priya: marking this thread for postmortem owner @devon. please capture timeline and follow-up action items (RMA cadence, alert tuning for pre-kernel panic signs).

devon: will take postmortem. initial notes captured. thanks all for quick triage. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: PD-927361 status changed to resolved by @priya.

incident-bot: incident closed at 2748003620.
